sourceDate.text: 高宗自以李氏老子之後也
老子（春秋晚期傳統年代）

units.zh: 聲無形而樂有器。
units.en: Sound is formless, yet music requires instruments.
units.literal: Sound has no form, yet music has instruments.

units.zh: 古之作樂者，知夫器之必有弊，而聲不可以言傳，懼夫器失而聲遂亡也，乃多為之法以著之。
units.en: Ancient composers knew instruments wear out and sound cannot be passed on in speech; lest instruments vanish and sound with them, they devised many ways to fix it in writing.
units.literal: The ancients who made music knew that instruments must eventually fail and that sound cannot be handed down in words; fearing that when instruments were lost sound would perish, they devised many methods to record it.

units.zh: 故始求聲者以律，而造律者以黍。
units.en: Those who first pursued tone turned to pitch pipes; those who forged pitch pipes took millet as their measure.
units.literal: Therefore those who first sought sound used pitch pipes, and those who made pitch pipes used millet.

units.zh: 自一黍之廣，積而為分、寸；
units.en: From the width of a single millet grain, one accumulates fen and cun.
units.literal: From the breadth of one millet grain, accumulated into fen and cun.

units.zh: 一黍之多，積而為龠、合；
units.en: From the capacity of one millet grain, one accumulates yue and he.
units.literal: From the volume of one millet grain, accumulated into yue and he.

units.zh: 一黍之重，積而為銖、兩。
units.en: From the weight of one millet grain, one accumulates zhu and liang.
units.literal: From the weight of one millet grain, accumulated into zhu and liang.

units.zh: 此造律之本也。
units.en: Such is the foundation of pitch-pipe manufacture.
units.literal: This is the root of making pitch pipes.

units.zh: 故為之長短之法，而著之於度；
units.en: They codified rules of length and fixed them in the standard of length.
units.literal: Therefore they made methods of long and short and recorded them in measures of length.

units.zh: 為之多少之法，而著之於量；
units.en: They codified rules of quantity and fixed them in the standard of capacity.
units.literal: They made methods of more and less and recorded them in measures of capacity.

units.zh: 為之輕重之法，而著之於權衡。
units.en: They codified rules of weight and fixed them in balances and steelyards.
units.literal: They made methods of light and heavy and recorded them in balances and steelyards.

units.zh: 是三物者，亦必有時而弊，則又總其法而著之於數。
units.en: These three standards too must eventually fail; they therefore summed their rules and committed them to number.
units.literal: These three things too must in time fail; then they gathered their methods together and recorded them in numbers.

units.zh: 使其分寸、龠合、銖兩皆起於黃鍾，然後律、度、量、衡相用為表裏，使得律者可以制度、量、衡，因度、量、衡亦可以制律。
units.en: Fen, cun, yue, he, zhu, and liang all derived from the Yellow Bell; pitch pipes, length, capacity, and weight then served as mutual inner and outer measures—whoever held the pipes could derive the rest, and from length, capacity, and weight one could likewise derive the pipes.
units.literal: They made fen, cun, yue, he, zhu, and liang all arise from the Yellow Bell; then pitch pipes, length, capacity, and weight were used as inner and outer counterparts, so that one who had pitch pipes could make length, capacity, and weight, and by length, capacity, and weight one could also make pitch pipes.

units.zh: 不幸而皆亡，則推其法數而制之，用其長短、多少、輕重以相參考。
units.en: Should all be lost, one could still reconstruct them from their numerical rules, cross-checking length, capacity, and weight.
units.literal: If unhappily all were lost, then one deduced from their numerical methods to make them, using their long and short, more and less, light and heavy for mutual reference.

units.zh: 四者既同，而聲必至，聲至后樂可作矣。
units.en: Once the four agreed, tone would surely be recovered; with tone restored, music could be composed.
units.literal: When the four were alike, sound was bound to arrive; once sound arrived, music could then be made.

units.zh: 夫物用於有形而必弊，聲藏於無形而不竭，以有數之法求無形之聲，其法具存。
units.en: Material things in visible form wear out; sound dwelling in the invisible does not exhaust itself—seek the formless through numbered rules, and the rules endure entire.
units.literal: Things used in what has form must fail; sound hidden in what has no form is inexhaustible—using methods that have number to seek sound that has no form, the methods remain fully preserved.

units.zh: 無作則已，苟有作者，雖去聖人於千萬歲後，無不得焉。
units.en: If none undertakes the task, so be it; yet whoever does, though ten thousand years from the sages, need miss nothing.
units.literal: If there is no making, so be it; but if there is a maker, though separated from the sages by ten thousand years, nothing is unobtainable.

units.zh: 此古之君子知物之終始，而憂世之慮深，其多為之法而丁寧纖悉，可謂至矣。
units.en: The ancients, knowing how things begin and end and anxious for posterity, multiplied methods with painstaking detail—nothing could exceed it.
units.literal: Thus the gentlemen of old, knowing things' beginning and end and deeply concerned for the age, made many methods with meticulous care—one may call this utmost.

units.zh: 三代既亡，禮樂失其本，至其聲器、有司之守，亦以散亡。
units.en: When the Three Dynasties ended, rites and music lost their foundation; even instruments and the officials charged with them dispersed and vanished.
units.literal: After the Three Dynasties perished, rites and music lost their root; even their sounding instruments and the keepers among the officials scattered and were lost.

units.zh: 自漢以來，歷代莫不有樂，作者各因其所學，雖清濁高下時有不同，然不能出於法數。
units.en: Since Han every dynasty had music; each maker drew on his own training; pitch might vary, yet none escaped the numerical system.
units.literal: From Han onward every age had music; each composer followed his own learning; though clear and muddy, high and low, differed at times, none could depart from numerical method.

units.zh: 至其所以用於郊廟、朝廷，以接人神之歡，其金石之響，歌舞之容，則各因其功業治亂之所起，而本其風俗之所由。
units.en: For music at suburban rites and court, where men and spirits meet in joy, the clang of metal and stone and the form of dance reflected each dynasty's rise or fall and the customs from which they sprang.
units.literal: As for what was used at suburban altars and in the court to join the joy of men and spirits, the resonance of metal and stone and the bearing of song and dance each followed whether merit and disorder had arisen, rooted in the customs whence they came.

units.zh: 自漢、魏之亂，晉遷江南，中國遂沒於夷狄。
units.en: After the chaos of Han and Wei, Jin retreated to the south; the heartland fell to northern peoples.
units.literal: From the disorders of Han and Wei, Jin moved south of the Yangtze, and the central lands were submerged by barbarians.

units.zh: 至隋滅陳，始得其樂器，稍欲因而有作，而時君褊迫，不足以堪其事也。
units.en: Sui's conquest of Chen recovered Chen instruments and stirred hopes of renewal, but the reigning emperor was too cramped in means to finish the work.
units.literal: When Sui destroyed Chen it at last obtained their musical instruments and wished somewhat to build upon them, but the ruler of the time was narrow and pressed, insufficient to bear the task.

units.zh: 是時鄭譯、牛弘、辛彥之、何妥、蔡子元、于普明之徒，皆名知樂，相與譔定。
units.en: Zheng Yi, Niu Hong, Xin Yanzhi, He Tuo, Cai Ziyuan, Yu Puming, and others—all celebrated masters—jointly drafted the regulations.
units.literal: At that time Zheng Yi, Niu Hong, Xin Yanzhi, He Tuo, Cai Ziyuan, Yu Puming, and the like were all famed for knowing music and together compiled and fixed it.

units.zh: 依京房六十律，因而六之，為三百六十律，以當一歲之日，又以一律為七音，音為一調，凡十二律為八十四調，其說甚詳。
units.en: They took Jing Fang's sixty pipes, multiplied by six for three hundred sixty to match the year's days, assigned seven tones per pipe and one mode per tone, yielding eighty-four modes from twelve pipes—a treatise of great detail.
units.literal: Following Jing Fang's sixty pitch pipes, they multiplied by six to make three hundred sixty pipes to match the days of a year; again taking each pipe as seven tones and each tone as one mode, twelve pipes in all made eighty-four modes—the exposition was very detailed.

units.zh: 而終隋之世，所用者黃鍾一宮，五夏、二舞、登歌、房中等十四調而已。
units.en: Yet Sui in practice used only Yellow Bell in the palace mode—Five Summers, the two dances, ascent song, chamber pieces—fourteen modes altogether.
units.literal: Yet through the whole Sui age what was used was only the Yellow Bell palace mode, the Five Summers, the two dances, ascent song, chamber music, and fourteen modes in all.

units.zh: 記曰：「功成作樂。」
units.en: The Record states: "When achievement is complete, music is composed."
units.literal: The Record says: "When merit is accomplished, music is made."

units.zh: 蓋王者未作樂之時，必因其舊而用之。
units.en: Before a sovereign fashions new music, he necessarily continues the former repertoire.
units.literal: For before a king has made music he must use the old and employ it.

units.zh: 唐興即用隋樂。
units.en: Tang at its founding adopted Sui music outright.
units.literal: When Tang rose it at once used Sui music.

units.zh: 武德九年，始詔太常少卿祖孝孫、協律郎竇璡等定樂。
units.en: In Wude year 9 the throne ordered Vice Director Zu Xiaosun, Harmony-Regulating Gentleman Dou Jin, and colleagues to standardize the music.
units.literal: In the ninth year of Wude an edict first ordered Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zu Xiaosun, Harmony-Regulating Gentleman Dou Jin, and others to fix the music.

units.zh: 初，隋用黃鍾一宮，惟擊七鍾，其五鍾設而不擊，謂之啞鍾。
units.en: Initially Sui kept to Yellow Bell palace mode and struck only seven bells; five bells stood silent—"mute bells."
units.literal: At first Sui used the Yellow Bell palace mode alone, striking only seven bells; five bells were set up but not struck, called mute bells.

units.zh: 唐協律郎張文收乃依古斷竹為十二律，高祖命與孝孫吹調五鍾，叩之而應，由是十二鍾皆用。
units.en: Zhang Wenshou, Harmony-Regulating Gentleman, cut bamboo into twelve pipes by ancient rule; Gaozu had him and Xiaosun tune the five mute bells—they answered when struck, and all twelve bells came into use.
units.literal: Tang's Harmony-Regulating Gentleman Zhang Wenshou then followed the ancient method of cutting bamboo for twelve pitch pipes; Gaozu ordered him with Xiaosun to blow and tune the five bells; struck, they responded, and thereafter all twelve bells were used.

units.zh: 孝孫又以十二月旋相為六十聲、八十四調。
units.en: Xiaosun further derived sixty sounds and eighty-four modes by cyclically permuting the twelve months.
units.literal: Xiaosun further took the twelve months in rotating succession to make sixty sounds and eighty-four modes.

units.zh: 其法，因五音生二變，因變徵為正徵，因變宮為清宮。
units.en: The method generated two "altered" tones from the five; altered zhi became proper zhi, altered gong became clear gong.
units.literal: The method: from the five tones generate two alterations; from altered zhi derive proper zhi, from altered gong derive clear gong.

units.zh: 七音起黃鍾，終南呂，迭為綱紀。
units.en: Seven tones ran from Yellow Bell to Nanlü, alternating as structural threads.
units.literal: The seven tones begin at Yellow Bell and end at Nanlü, each in turn the warp and woof.

units.zh: 黃鍾之律，管長九寸，王於中宮土。
units.en: The Yellow Bell pipe measures nine cun and rules as earth at the central palace.
units.literal: The Yellow Bell pipe is nine cun long and reigns as central palace earth.

units.zh: 半之，四寸五分，與清宮合，五音之首也。
units.en: Halved to four cun five fen, it aligns with clear gong—the leading tone of the five.
units.literal: Halved, four cun five fen, it matches clear gong—the head of the five tones.

units.zh: 加以二變，循環無間。
units.en: With the two alterations added, the cycle closes without break.
units.literal: Adding the two alterations, the cycle is without gap.

units.zh: 故一宮、二商、三角、四變徵、五徵、六羽、七變宮，其聲繇濁至清為一均。
units.en: Thus: gong, shang, jue, altered zhi, zhi, yu, altered gong—pitch ascending from muddy to clear within one jun.
units.literal: Thus one gong, two shang, three jue, four altered zhi, five zhi, six yu, seven altered gong—from muddy to clear sound forms one jun.

units.zh: 凡十二宮調，皆正宮也。
units.en: All twelve gong modes count as proper gong.
units.literal: All twelve gong modes are proper gong modes.

units.zh: 正宮聲之下，無復濁音，故五音以宮為尊。
units.en: Proper gong admits no tone below it in pitch; hence gong ranks first among the five.
units.literal: Below the proper gong tone there is no further muddy sound; therefore among the five tones gong is honored.

units.zh: 十二商調，調有下聲一，謂宮也。
units.en: Each of the twelve shang modes carries one underpinning tone—gong.
units.literal: The twelve shang modes each have one lower tone, called gong.

units.zh: 十二角調，調有下聲二，宮、商也。
units.en: Each jue mode carries two underpinning tones—gong and shang.
units.literal: The twelve jue modes each have two lower tones, gong and shang.

units.zh: 十二徵調，調有下聲三，宮、商、角也。
units.en: Each zhi mode carries three underpinning tones—gong, shang, and jue.
units.literal: The twelve zhi modes each have three lower tones, gong, shang, and jue.

units.zh: 十二羽調，調有下聲四，宮、商、角、徵也。
units.en: Each yu mode carries four underpinning tones—gong through zhi.
units.literal: The twelve yu modes each have four lower tones, gong, shang, jue, and zhi.

units.zh: 十二變徵調，居角音之後，正徵之前。
units.en: Twelve altered-zhi modes sit after jue and before proper zhi.
units.literal: The twelve altered-zhi modes stand after jue and before proper zhi.

units.zh: 十二變宮調，在羽音之後，清宮之前。
units.en: Twelve altered-gong modes sit after yu and before clear gong.
units.literal: The twelve altered-gong modes stand after yu and before clear gong.

units.zh: 雅樂成調，無出七聲，本宮遞相用。
units.en: Court music forms its modes within seven tones, the home gong passing from one to the next.
units.literal: Elegant music in forming modes does not exceed seven tones; the root gong is used in succession.

units.zh: 唯樂章則隨律定均，合以笙、磬，節以鍾、鼓。
units.en: For actual pieces the jun follows the pipes, joined with mouth-organ and stone chimes, paced by bells and drums.
units.literal: Only for musical sections are jun fixed according to the pipes, joined with sheng and qing, regulated by bells and drums.

units.zh: 樂既成，奏之。
units.en: Once the music stood complete, it was performed.
units.literal: When the music was complete, it was performed.

units.zh: 太宗謂侍臣曰：「古者聖人沿情以作樂，國之興衰，未必由此。」
units.en: Taizong told his ministers: "Sages of old shaped music from human feeling; a dynasty's fortune need not hinge on it."
units.literal: Taizong said to his attendants: "The ancients' sages followed feeling to make music; a state's rise and fall need not come from this."

units.zh: 御史大夫杜淹曰：「陳將亡也，有玉樹後庭花，齊將亡也，有伴侶曲，聞者悲泣，所謂亡國之音哀以思。
units.en: Censor-in-Chief Du Yan replied: "Chen on the brink had Jade Tree in the Rear Courtyard; Qi had the Companion Piece—listeners wept. Such is the 'music of a dying realm,' grief within longing.
units.literal: Censor-in-Chief Du Yan said: "When Chen was about to perish there was Jade Tree in the Rear Courtyard; when Qi was about to perish there was the Companion Piece—hearers wept; this is what is called the sound of a perishing state, mournful and longing.

units.zh: 以是觀之，亦樂之所起。」
units.en: Seen this way, music too can herald ruin."
units.literal: Viewed thus, music too is where such things begin."

units.zh: 帝曰：「夫聲之所感，各因人之哀樂。
units.en: The emperor said: "Sound moves each listener according to his own sorrow or joy.
units.literal: The emperor said: "What sound stirs each person follows his own grief or joy.

units.zh: 將亡之政，其民苦，故聞以悲。
units.en: Where rule is failing the people are wretched; hearing such songs, they grieve.
units.literal: In a government about to perish the people suffer, so on hearing they are mournful.

units.zh: 今玉樹、伴侶之曲尚存，為公奏之，知必不悲。」
units.en: Those tunes survive; play them for you now and you will not weep."
units.literal: The Jade Tree and Companion Piece songs still exist; played for you, they will surely not move you to grief."

units.zh: 尚書右丞魏徵進曰：「孔子稱：『樂云樂云，鍾鼓云乎哉。』
units.en: Wei Zheng, Right Vice Director, said: "Confucius said: 'Music, music—is it only bells and drums?'
units.literal: Right Vice Director Wei Zheng advanced and said: "Confucius said: 'Music, music—is it merely bells and drums?

units.zh: 樂在人和，不在音也。」
units.en: Music rests in concord among people, not in notes."
units.literal: Music lies in human harmony, not in sound."

units.zh: 十一年，張文收復請重正餘樂，帝不許，曰：「朕聞人和則樂和，隋末喪亂，雖改音律而樂不和。
units.en: In year 11 Zhang Wenshou again asked to retune the remaining repertoire; the emperor refused: "When the people are at peace, music harmonizes; Sui's final chaos left pipes retuned yet music discordant.
units.literal: In the eleventh year Zhang Wenshou again requested to re-standardize the remaining music; the emperor did not permit it, saying: "I have heard that when people are harmonious, music is harmonious; at the end of Sui there was chaos and ruin—though pitch pipes were changed, music was not harmonious.

units.zh: 若百姓安樂，金石自諧矣。」
units.en: Let the common people live in ease, and metal and stone will accord without further effort."
units.literal: If the hundred surnames are secure and joyful, metal and stone will harmonize of themselves."

units.zh: 文收既定樂，復鑄銅律三百六十、銅斛二、銅秤二、銅甌十四、秤尺一。
units.en: Once Wenshou had settled the music, he cast three hundred sixty copper pitch pipes, two copper hu, two steelyards, fourteen copper ou, and one measuring rod for the steelyard.
units.literal: After Wenshou had fixed the music, he further cast three hundred sixty copper pitch pipes, two copper hu, two copper steelyards, fourteen copper ou, and one steelyard-measure rod.

units.zh: 斛左右耳與臀皆方，積十而登，以至於斛，與古玉尺、玉斗同。
units.en: The hu's ears and base were square; capacities stacked by tens to the hu, matching ancient jade measure and dipper.
units.literal: The hu's left and right ears and base were all square; tenfold accumulation ascended to the hu, matching the ancient jade foot-rule and jade dipper.

units.zh: 皆藏於太樂署。
units.en: All were kept in the Office of Great Music.
units.literal: All were stored in the Office of Great Music.

units.zh: 武后時，太常卿武延秀以為奇玩，乃獻之。
units.en: Under Empress Wu, Director Wu Yanxiu treated them as marvels and presented them to the throne.
units.literal: In Empress Wu's time Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wu Yanxiu took them for curios and presented them.

units.zh: 及將考中宗廟樂，有司奏請出之，而秤尺已亡，其跡猶存，以常用度量校之，尺當六之五，量、衡皆三之一。
units.en: For Zhongzong's temple music the offices requested them; the measuring rod was gone though its marks remained—against present measures the foot was five-sixths, capacity and weight one-third each.
units.literal: When they were to examine Zhongzong's temple music the authorities memorialized to bring them out, but the steelyard rod was already lost; its traces remained; comparing with current measures, the foot was five-sixths, capacity and weight each one-third.

units.zh: 至肅宗時，山東人魏延陵得律一，因中官李輔國獻之，云：「太常諸樂調皆下，不合黃鍾，請悉更制諸鍾磬。」
units.en: Under Suzong, Wei Yanling of Shandong found a pipe and presented it through Li Fuguo, claiming: "Court tunes all ran low against Yellow Bell and all bells and stones should be remade."
units.literal: By Suzong's time Shandong man Wei Yanling obtained one pitch pipe and through eunuch Li Fuguo presented it, saying: "All tunes of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices are too low and do not match Yellow Bell; please entirely remake all bells and chime-stones."

units.zh: 帝以為然，乃悉取太常諸樂器入于禁中，更加磨剡，凡二十五日而成。
units.en: The emperor agreed, brought every Court instrument within the palace, filed and polished them, and finished in twenty-five days.
units.literal: The emperor thought it right and took all Court instruments into the inner palace, further grinding and filing them; in twenty-five days it was done.

units.zh: 御三殿觀之，以還太常，然以漢律考之，黃鍾乃太簇也，當時議者以為非是。
units.en: He inspected them in the Three Halls and returned them; tested against Han standards, Yellow Bell matched Taicu—critics deemed this mistaken.
units.literal: He viewed them in the Three Halls and returned them to the Court; yet tested against Han pipes, Yellow Bell proved to be Taicu; contemporaries held this wrong.

units.zh: 其後黃巢之亂，樂工逃散，金奏皆亡。
units.en: After Huang Chao's revolt musicians scattered; all metal music was lost.
units.literal: Afterward in Huang Chao's rebellion musicians fled and scattered; metal performances were all lost.

units.zh: 昭宗即位，將謁郊廟，有司不知樂縣制度。
units.en: Zhaozong, on accession, prepared suburban rites; officials no longer knew how to set the music stands.
units.literal: When Zhaozong took the throne he was about to visit the suburban altars; the authorities did not know the music-stand system.

units.zh: 太常博士殷盈孫按周法以算數除鎛鍾輕重高卬，黃鍾九寸五分，倍應鍾三寸三分半，凡四十八等。
units.en: Doctor Yin Yingsun, by Zhou arithmetic, calculated bo-bell weight and pitch—Yellow Bell at nine cun five fen, doubled Ying Bell at three cun three and a half fen, forty-eight grades total.
units.literal: Court of Imperial Sacrifices Doctor Yin Yingsun by Zhou methods used calculation to divide the weight and height of bo bells—Yellow Bell nine cun five fen, doubled Ying Bell three cun three and a half fen, forty-eight grades in all.

units.zh: 圖上口項之量及徑衡之圍。
units.en: He charted mouth and crown dimensions and stem and crossbar circumference.
units.literal: He diagrammed the measure of mouth and crown and the girth of stem and crossbar.

units.zh: 乃命鑄鎛鍾十二，編鍾二百四十。
units.en: He ordered twelve bo bells and two hundred forty chime-bells cast.
units.literal: He then ordered twelve bo bells cast and two hundred forty serial bells.

units.zh: 宰相張濬為脩奉樂縣使，求知聲者，得處士蕭承訓等，校石磬，合而擊拊之，音遂諧。
units.en: Zhang Jun, chief minister, as commissioner for the music stands found masters such as Xiao Chengxun, tuned the stone chimes, and achieved harmony.
units.literal: Chief Minister Zhang Jun served as Commissioner for Repairing and Presenting the Music Stands; seeking those who knew sound, he obtained Recluse Xiao Chengxun and others, calibrated stone chimes, joined and struck them, and the tones harmonized.

units.zh: 唐為國而作樂之制尤簡，高祖、太宗即用隋樂與孝孫、文收所定而已。
units.en: Tang's state-music regulations were notably spare: Gaozu and Taizong kept Sui music plus Xiaosun's and Wenshou's revisions.
units.literal: Tang's system for making state music was especially simple: Gaozu and Taizong used only Sui music and what Xiaosun and Wenshou had fixed.

units.zh: 其後世所更者，樂章舞曲。
units.en: Later changes touched chiefly lyrics and dances.
units.literal: What later ages changed were musical sections and dance pieces.

units.zh: 至于昭宗，始得盈孫焉，故其議論罕所發明。
units.en: Not until Zhaozong and Yin Yingsun did theory find voice again; earlier discourse seldom innovated.
units.literal: Only by Zhaozong did Yin Yingsun appear; hence their discussions rarely advanced new doctrine.

units.zh: 若其樂歌廟舞，用於當世者，可以考也。
units.en: Their temple hymns, dances, and contemporary usage can still be traced.
units.literal: As for their hymns, temple dances, and what was used in their own time, these may be examined.

units.zh: 樂縣之制。
units.en: Regulations for music stands.
units.literal: The system of music stands.

units.zh: 宮縣四面，天子用之。
units.en: Palace stands on four sides were reserved for the Son of Heaven.
units.literal: Palace stands on four sides—the Son of Heaven used them.

units.zh: 若祭祀，則前祀二日，太樂令設縣於壇南內壝之外，北嚮。
units.en: For sacrifice, two days prior the Director of Great Music erects stands south of the altar within the inner rampart, facing north.
units.literal: For sacrifice, two days before the rite the Director of Great Music sets the stands south of the altar within the inner enclosure, facing north.

units.zh: 東方、西方，磬虡起北，鍾虡次之；
units.en: East and west: stone-chime frames begin at the north, bell frames follow.
units.literal: East and west: qing frames start from the north, bell frames next.

units.zh: 南方、北方，磬虡起西，鍾虡次之。
units.en: South and north: stone-chime frames begin at the west, bell frames follow.
units.literal: South and north: qing frames start from the west, bell frames next.

units.zh: 鎛鍾十有二，在十二辰之位。
units.en: Twelve bo bells occupy the twelve chronogram stations.
units.literal: Twelve bo bells stand at the twelve chronogram positions.

units.zh: 樹雷鼓於北縣之內、道之左右，植建鼓於四隅。
units.en: Thunder drums stand within the northern frame, flanking the path; establishment drums at the four corners.
units.literal: Thunder drums are set within the northern stands, left and right of the path; establishment drums are planted at the four corners.

units.zh: 置柷、敔於縣內，柷在右，敔在左。
units.en: Zhu and yu sit inside the frame—zhu right, yu left.
units.literal: Zhu and yu are placed within the stands—zhu on the right, yu on the left.

units.zh: 設歌鍾、歌磬於壇上，南方北向。
units.en: Song bells and song chimes are placed on the altar, the southern tier facing north.
units.literal: Song bells and song chimes are set on the altar, the southern row facing north.

units.zh: 磬虡在西，鍾虡在東。
units.en: Stone-chime frames west, bell frames east.
units.literal: Qing frames on the west, bell frames on the east.

units.zh: 琴、瑟、箏、筑皆一，當磬虡之次，匏、竹在下。
units.en: One each of qin, se, zheng, and zhu beside the stone frames; gourd and bamboo below.
units.literal: Qin, se, zheng, and zhu each one, next after the qing frames; gourd and bamboo below.

units.zh: 凡天神之類，皆以雷鼓；
units.en: Heavenly spirits are accompanied by thunder drums.
units.literal: For all classes of heavenly spirits, thunder drums are used.

units.zh: 地祇之類，皆以靈鼓；
units.en: Earthly spirits by spirit drums.
units.literal: For all classes of earthly spirits, spirit drums are used.

units.zh: 人鬼之類，皆以路鼓。
units.en: Human ghosts by road drums.
units.literal: For all classes of human ghosts, road drums are used.

units.zh: 其設於庭，則在南，而登歌者在堂。
units.en: In the courtyard the stands lie southward; ascent singers remain in the hall.
units.literal: When set in the courtyard they are in the south, while ascent singers are in the hall.

units.zh: 若朝會，則加鍾磬十二虡，設鼓吹十二案於建鼓之外。
units.en: At court audiences twelve more bell and chime frames appear, with twelve wind-and-drum tables beyond the establishment drums.
units.literal: For court audiences, twelve additional bell and qing frames are added, and twelve tables of wind-and-percussion music are set outside the establishment drums.

units.zh: 案設羽葆鼓一，大鼓一，金錞一，歌、簫、笳皆二。
units.en: Each table holds one feather-canopied drum, one great drum, one bronze chime, and pairs of song-pipe, xiao, and horn.
units.literal: Each table has one feather-canopied drum, one great drum, one bronze cymbal, and two each of song-pipe, xiao, and horn.

units.zh: 登歌，鍾、磬各一虡，節鼓一，歌者四人，琴、瑟、箏、筑皆一，在堂上；
units.en: Ascent song: one bell frame, one chime frame, one marking drum, four singers, qin, se, zheng, and zhu on the hall.
units.literal: For ascent song, one frame each of bells and chimes, one marking drum, four singers, one each of qin, se, zheng, and zhu on the hall.

units.zh: 笙、和、簫、篪、塤皆一，在堂下。
units.en: Sheng, he, xiao, chi, and xun—one each below the hall.
units.literal: Sheng, he, xiao, chi, and xun each one, below the hall.

units.zh: 若皇后享先蠶，則設十二大磬，以當辰位，而無路鼓。
units.en: For the empress's First Silkworm rite, twelve great stone chimes match the chronogram stations, without road drums.
units.literal: When the empress performs the First Silkworm rite, twelve great qing are set to match the chronogram positions, without road drums.

units.zh: 軒縣三面，皇太子用之。
units.en: Pavilion stands on three sides served the heir apparent.
units.literal: Pavilion stands on three sides—the heir apparent used them.

units.zh: 若釋奠于文宣王、武成王，亦用之。
units.en: Libations to Confucius and the Martial Completion King used them as well.
units.literal: For libation at Confucius and at the Martial Completion King, these too were used.

units.zh: 其制，去宮縣之南面。
units.en: Its layout omits the palace stand's southern side.
units.literal: Its system removes the southern face of the palace stands.

units.zh: 判縣二面，唐之舊禮，祭風伯、雨師、五嶽、四瀆用之。
units.en: Two-sided adjudged stands served Tang's old rites to wind, rain, the Five Peaks, and the Four Rivers.
units.literal: Adjudged stands on two faces—Tang's old rite for sacrificing to the Wind Lord, Rain Master, Five Sacred Peaks, and Four Rivers.

units.zh: 其制，去軒縣之北面。
units.en: Its layout omits the pavilion stand's northern side.
units.literal: Its system removes the northern face of the pavilion stands.

units.zh: 皆植建鼓於東北、西北二隅。
units.en: Establishment drums stand at the northeast and northwest corners.
units.literal: Establishment drums are planted at the northeast and northwest corners.

units.zh: 特縣，去判縣之西面，或陳於階間，有其制而無所用。
units.en: Special stands drop the adjudged stand's west face or sit between stairways—prescribed yet never employed.
units.literal: Special stands remove the western face of the adjudged stands, or are arrayed between steps; the system exists but was unused.

units.zh: 凡橫者為簨，植者為虡。
units.en: Horizontal members are beams; upright supports are frames.
units.literal: What lies horizontal is the beam; what stands vertical is the frame.

units.zh: 虡以縣鍾磬，皆十有六，周人謂之一堵，而唐人謂之一虡。
units.en: Frames hold bells and chimes, sixteen per unit—Zhou called one unit a "wall," Tang called it a frame.
units.literal: Frames suspend bells and chimes, each sixteen in all; Zhou people called one set a "wall," Tang people called it one frame.

units.zh: 自隋以前，宮縣二十虡。
units.en: Before Sui, palace stands employed twenty frames.
units.literal: Before Sui, palace stands used twenty frames.

units.zh: 及隋平陳，得梁故事用三十六虡，遂用之。
units.en: Sui's conquest of Chen recovered Liang practice—thirty-six frames—and so employed them.
units.literal: When Sui pacified Chen it obtained Liang precedent and used thirty-six frames, and so employed them.

units.zh: 唐初因隋舊，用三十六虡。
units.en: Early Tang retained Sui's thirty-six frames.
units.literal: Early Tang followed Sui's old usage with thirty-six frames.

units.zh: 高宗蓬萊宮成，增用七十二虡。
units.en: After Gaozong's Penglai Palace rose, the count doubled to seventy-two frames.
units.literal: When Gaozong's Penglai Palace was completed, use was increased to seventy-two frames.

units.zh: 至武后時省之。
units.en: Empress Wu later cut them back.
units.literal: By Empress Wu's time they were reduced.

units.zh: 開元定禮，始依古著為二十虡。
units.en: Kaiyuan ritual reform restored the ancient twenty frames.
units.literal: When Kaiyuan fixed the rites, they first followed the ancient record of twenty frames.

units.zh: 至昭宗時，宰相張濬已修樂縣，乃言，舊制，太清宮、南北郊、社稷及諸殿廷用二十虡，而太廟、含元殿用三十六虡，濬以為非古，而廟廷狹隘，不能容三十六，乃復用二十虡。
units.en: Under Zhaozong, Zhang Jun—having restored the stands—noted that suburban rites and most halls used twenty frames while the Ancestral Temple and Hanyuan Hall used thirty-six; deeming this unancient and the courts too cramped, he reverted to twenty.
units.literal: By Zhaozong's time Chief Minister Zhang Jun had already repaired the music stands and said: under the old system the Taiqing Palace, southern and northern suburbs, altars of soil and grain, and various palace halls used twenty frames, while the Imperial Ancestral Temple and Hanyuan Hall used thirty-six; Jun held this unancient, and the temple and hall courts were narrow and could not contain thirty-six, so twenty frames were restored.

units.zh: 而鍾虡四，以當甲丙庚壬，磬虡四，以當乙丁辛癸，與開元禮異，而不知其改制之時。
units.en: Four bell frames matched jia-bing-geng-ren; four chime frames matched yi-ding-xin-gui—unlike Kaiyuan usage, though when the change occurred is unknown.
units.literal: Bell frames four, matching jia, bing, geng, ren; chime frames four, matching yi, ding, xin, gui—differing from Kaiyuan rites, the time of the change unknown.

units.zh: 或說以鍾磬應陰陽之位，此禮經所不著。
units.en: Some claimed bells and chimes mapped yin-yang stations—the classics record no such rule.
units.literal: Some say bells and chimes correspond to yin-yang positions—this the ritual classics do not record.

units.zh: 凡樂八音，自漢以來，惟金以鍾定律呂，故其制度最詳，其餘七者，史官不記。
units.en: Since Han only the metal class—bells fixing pitch—was fully documented; historians left the other seven sounds vague.
units.literal: Of music's eight sounds, from Han onward only metal, through bells fixing pitch pipes, has the most detailed system; the other seven the historiographers did not record.

units.zh: 至唐，獨宮縣與登歌、鼓吹十二案樂器有數，其餘皆略而不著，而其物名具在。
units.en: Tang records give counts for palace stands, ascent song, and the twelve wind tables; other instruments are named but not tallied.
units.literal: By Tang, only palace stands, ascent song, and the twelve wind-and-drum tables had numbered instruments; the rest were sketched briefly though their names remain.

units.zh: 八音：一曰金，為鎛鍾，為編鍾，為歌鍾，為錞，為鐃，為鐲，為鐸。
units.en: Eight sounds: I. Metal—bo bells, serial bells, song bells, cymbals, naos, bozhuo, duo.
units.literal: The eight sounds: first metal—bo bells, serial bells, song bells, cymbals, naos, bozhuo, and duo.

units.zh: 二曰石，為大磬，為編磬，為歌磬。
units.en: II. Stone—great chimes, serial chimes, song chimes.
units.literal: Second stone—great qing, serial qing, song qing.

units.zh: 三曰土，為壎，為嘂，嘂，大壎也。
units.en: III. Earth—xun and jiao (the great xun).
units.literal: Third earth—xun and jiao; jiao is the great xun.

units.zh: 四曰革，為雷鼓，為靈鼓，為路鼓，皆有鼗；
units.en: IV. Hide—thunder, spirit, and road drums, each with rattles.
units.literal: Fourth hide—thunder drum, spirit drum, and road drum, all with rattles.

units.zh: 為建鼓，為鼗鼓，為縣鼓，為節鼓，為拊，為相。
units.en: Also establishment drum, tao drum, suspended drum, marking drum, clapper, and xiang.
units.literal: Establishment drum, tao drum, suspended drum, marking drum, clapper, and xiang.

units.zh: 五曰絲，為琴，為瑟，為頌瑟，頌瑟，箏也；
units.en: V. Silk—qin, se, ode-se (i.e., zheng).
units.literal: Fifth silk—qin, se, ode se; ode se is zheng.

units.zh: 為阮咸，為筑。
units.en: Ruanxian and zhu.
units.literal: Ruanxian and zhu.

units.zh: 六曰木，為柷，為敔，為雅，為應。
units.en: VI. Wood—zhu, yu, ya, ying.
units.literal: Sixth wood—zhu, yu, ya, and ying.

units.zh: 七曰匏，為笙，為竽，為巢，巢，大笙也；
units.en: VII. Gourd—sheng, yu, chao (great sheng).
units.literal: Seventh gourd—sheng, yu, and chao; chao is the great sheng.

units.zh: 為和，和，小笙也。
units.en: He—the small sheng.
units.literal: He; he is the small sheng.

units.zh: 八曰竹，為簫，為管，為篪，為笛，為舂牘。
units.en: VIII. Bamboo—xiao, guan, chi, di, chundu.
units.literal: Eighth bamboo—xiao, guan, chi, di, and chundu.

units.zh: 此其樂器也。
units.en: Such were the instruments.
units.literal: These are the musical instruments.

units.zh: 初，祖孝孫已定樂，乃曰大樂與天地同和者也，製十二和，以法天之成數，號大唐雅樂：一曰豫和，二曰順和，三曰永和，四曰肅和，五曰雍和，六曰壽和，七曰太和，八曰舒和，九曰昭和，十曰休和，十一曰正和，十二曰承和。
units.en: Zu Xiaosun, having set the music, declared great music one with Heaven and Earth and fashioned twelve harmonies after Heaven's complete number, calling them Great Tang Elegant Music: Yuhe, Shunhe, Yonghe (Eternal Harmony), Suhe, Yonghe (Concordant Harmony), Shouhe, Taihe, Shuhe, Zhaohe, Xiuhe, Zhenghe, and Chenghe.
units.literal: At first Zu Xiaosun had already fixed the music and said: great music is of one harmony with Heaven and Earth; he made twelve harmonies to match Heaven's completion number, titled Great Tang Elegant Music: first Yühe, second Shunhe, third Yonghe, fourth Suhe, fifth Yonghe-yong, sixth Shouhe, seventh Taihe, eighth Shuhe, ninth Zhaohe, tenth Xiuhe, eleventh Zhenghe, twelfth Chenghe.

units.zh: 用於郊廟、朝廷，以和人神。
units.en: They served suburban altars and court to unite men and spirits.
units.literal: Used at suburban altars and court to harmonize men and spirits.

units.zh: 孝孫已卒，張文收以為十二和之制未備，乃詔有司釐定，而文收考正律呂，起居郎呂才叶其聲音，樂曲遂備。
units.en: After Xiaosun's death Wenshou found the twelve harmonies unfinished; the throne ordered revision—Wenshou tuned the pipes, Lü Cai matched the tones, and the repertoire was complete.
units.literal: After Xiaosun died, Zhang Wenshou held the twelve harmonies incomplete and an edict ordered the authorities to fix them; Wenshou corrected pitch pipes, Attendant Gentleman Lü Cai harmonized the tones, and the musical pieces were complete.

units.zh: 自高宗以後，稍更其曲名。
units.en: From Gaozong on, piece titles shifted.
units.literal: From Gaozong onward the piece names were gradually changed.

units.zh: 開元定禮，始復遵用孝孫十二和，其著于禮者：
units.en: Kaiyuan ritual code restored Xiaosun's twelve harmonies, of which the rites record:
units.literal: When Kaiyuan fixed the rites they first again followed Xiaosun's twelve harmonies; those recorded in the rites:

units.zh: 一曰豫和，以降天神。
units.en: I. Yühe—to summon heavenly spirits.
units.literal: First Yühe, to bring down heavenly spirits.

units.zh: 冬至祀圓丘，上辛祈穀，孟夏雩，季秋享明堂，朝日，夕月，巡狩告于圓丘，燔柴告至，封祀太山，類于上帝，皆以圜鍾為宮，三奏；
units.en: Round Mound winter solstice, grain prayers, summer rain rite, Bright Hall autumn rite, sun and moon sacrifices, tour announcements, Feng and Shan—all take round-bell as gong, three plays.
units.literal: Winter solstice sacrifice at the Round Mound, first xin prayer for grain, summer yu rain rite, autumnal equinox Bright Hall, sunrise and moonset rites, imperial tour announcing at the Round Mound, fire offering on arrival, Feng on Mount Tai, classification to the Supreme Lord—all use the round-bell as gong, three performances.

units.zh: 黃鍾為角，太簇為徵，姑洗為羽，各一奏，文舞六成。
units.en: Yellow Bell as jue, Taizu as zhi, Guxian as yu, one play each; civil dance six sections.
units.literal: Yellow Bell as jue, Taizu as zhi, Guxian as yu, each one performance; civil dance six formations.

units.zh: 五郊迎氣，黃帝以黃鍾為宮，赤帝以函鍾為徵，白帝以太簇為商，黑帝以南呂為羽，青帝以姑洗為角，皆文舞六成。
units.en: In the five suburban rites for welcoming the qi, the Yellow Emperor used Yellow Bell as gong, the Red Emperor used Hanzhong as zhi, the White Emperor used Taicu as shang, the Black Emperor used Nanlu as yu, and the Blue Emperor used Guxian as jue; all used six sections of civil dance.
units.literal: Five suburbs welcoming qi: Yellow Emperor takes Yellow Bell as gong; Red Emperor Hánzhong as zhi; White Emperor Taizu as shang; Black Emperor Nanlü as yu; Blue Emperor Guxian as jue—all civil dance six formations.

units.zh: 二曰順和，以降地祇。
units.en: II. Shunhe—for earthly spirits.
units.literal: Second Shunhe, to bring down earthly spirits.

units.zh: 夏至祭方丘，孟冬祭神州地祇，春秋社，巡狩告社，宜于社，禪社首，皆以函鍾為宮，太簇為角，姑洗為徵，南呂為羽，各三奏，文舞八成。
units.en: Square Mound summer solstice, Land and Grain winter rite, spring and autumn she, tour she announcements—Hánzhong gong, Taizu jue, Guxian zhi, Nanlü yu, three plays each; civil dance eight sections.
units.literal: Summer solstice at the Square Mound, winter at the Altars of Land and Grain, spring and autumn she, tour announcements at the she altar, She at She Mountain—all use Hánzhong as gong, Taizu as jue, Guxian as zhi, Nanlü as yu, three each; civil dance eight formations.

units.zh: 望于山川，以蕤賓為宮，三奏。
units.en: Mountain and river sacrifices use Ruibin as gong, three plays.
units.literal: Sacrifice to mountains and rivers uses Ruibin as gong, three performances.

units.zh: 三曰永和，以降人鬼。
units.en: III. Yonghe—for human spirits.
units.literal: Third Yonghe, to bring down human ghosts.

units.zh: 時享、禘祫，有事而告謁于廟，皆以黃鍾為宮，三奏；
units.en: Seasonal temple offerings and di/xia rites use Yellow Bell as gong, three plays.
units.literal: Seasonal offerings and di and xia sacrifices, announcements at the temple when there is business—all use Yellow Bell as gong, three performances.

units.zh: 大呂為角，太簇為徵，應鍾為羽，各二奏。
units.en: Dalu as jue, Taizu as zhi, Yingzhong as yu, two each.
units.literal: Dalu as jue, Taizu as zhi, Yingzhong as yu, two each.

units.zh: 文舞九成。
units.en: Civil dance nine sections.
units.literal: Civil dance nine formations.

units.zh: 祀先農，皇太子釋奠，皆以姑洗為宮，文舞三成；
units.en: First Farmer and heir apparent libations use Guxian as gong, civil dance three sections.
units.literal: Sacrifice to the First Farmer, heir apparent libation—all use Guxian as gong, civil dance three formations.

units.zh: 送神，各以其曲一成。
units.en: Spirit dismissal uses each piece once.
units.literal: Sending off the spirits, each with its piece one formation.

units.zh: 蜡兼天地人，以黃鍾奏豫和，蕤賓、姑洗、太簇奏順和，無射、夷則奏永和，六均皆一成以降神，而送神以豫和。
units.en: La rite unites heaven, earth, and man—Yühe on Yellow Bell, Shunhe on Ruibin, Guxian, and Taicu, Yonghe on Wuxie and Yize; six jun one play each for descent; dismissal returns to Yühe.
units.literal: The la rite joins heaven, earth, and man—Yellow Bell plays Yühe, Ruibin, Guxian, and Taicu play Shunhe, Wuxie and Yize play Yonghe; six jun each one formation to bring down spirits; sending off uses Yühe.

units.zh: 四曰肅和，登歌以奠玉帛。
units.en: IV. Suhe—ascent song presenting jade and silk.
units.literal: Fourth Suhe, ascent song to present jade and silk.

units.zh: 于天神，以大呂為宮；
units.en: To heavenly spirits: Dalu as gong.
units.literal: To heavenly spirits, Dalu as gong.

units.zh: 于地祇，以應鍾為宮；
units.en: To earthly spirits: Yingzhong as gong.
units.literal: To earthly spirits, Yingzhong as gong.

units.zh: 于宗廟，以圜鍾為宮；
units.en: To the ancestral temple: round-bell as gong.
units.literal: To the ancestral temple, round-bell as gong.

units.zh: 祀先農、釋奠，以南呂為宮；
units.en: First Farmer and libation: Nanlü as gong.
units.literal: First Farmer and libation, Nanlü as gong.

units.zh: 望于山川，以函鍾為宮。
units.en: Mountains and rivers: Hánzhong as gong.
units.literal: Mountains and rivers, Hánzhong as gong.

units.zh: 五曰雍和，凡祭祀以入俎。
units.en: V. Yong-yong—music when offerings enter the tray.
units.literal: Fifth Yonghe-yong, all sacrifices when entering the offering tray.

units.zh: 天神之俎，以黃鍾為宮；
units.en: Heavenly offering trays: Yellow Bell as gong.
units.literal: Heavenly spirits' tray, Yellow Bell as gong.

units.zh: 地祇之俎，以太簇為宮；
units.en: Earthly offering trays: Taizu as gong.
units.literal: Earthly spirits' tray, Taizu as gong.

units.zh: 人鬼之俎，以無射為宮。
units.en: Human-spirit trays: Wuxie as gong.
units.literal: Human ghosts' tray, Wuxie as gong.

units.zh: 又以徹豆。
units.en: Also for withdrawing the bean vessels.
units.literal: Also for withdrawing the beans.

units.zh: 凡祭祀，俎入之後，接神之曲亦如之。
units.en: After trays enter, the spirit-receiving pieces repeat the same modes.
units.literal: For all sacrifices, after the tray enters, the piece receiving the spirits is likewise.

units.zh: 六曰壽和，以酌獻、飲福。
units.en: VI. Shouhe—for libation pour and blessing cup.
units.literal: Sixth Shouhe, for pouring the libation and drinking the blessing.

units.zh: 以黃鍾為宮。
units.en: Yellow Bell as gong.
units.literal: Yellow Bell as gong.

units.zh: 七曰太和，以為行節。
units.en: VII. Taihe—for procession cadence.
units.literal: Seventh Taihe, for procession cadence.

units.zh: 亦以黃鍾為宮。
units.en: Also Yellow Bell as gong.
units.literal: Also Yellow Bell as gong.

units.zh: 凡祭祀，天子入門而即位，與其升降，至于還次，行則作，止則止。
units.en: At sacrifices the Son of Heaven's every step from gate to position and back—music plays while he moves, stops when he halts.
units.literal: For all sacrifices, when the Son of Heaven enters the gate and takes position, ascending and descending, until returning to place—walking it plays, stopping it ceases.

units.zh: 其在朝廷，天子將自內出，撞黃鍾之鍾，右五鍾應，乃奏之。
units.en: At court, before the emperor exits the inner palace, he strikes Yellow Bell; the five right bells answer, then Taihe plays.
units.literal: In court, when the Son of Heaven is about to emerge from within, he strikes the Yellow Bell bell; the five bells on the right respond, then it is performed.

units.zh: 其禮畢，興而入，撞蕤賓之鍾，左五鍾應，乃奏之。
units.en: When the rite ends and he re-enters, Ruibin is struck; the five left bells answer.
units.literal: When the rite ends and he rises to enter, he strikes the Ruibin bell; the five bells on the left respond, then it is performed.

units.zh: 皆以黃鍾為宮。
units.en: Both use Yellow Bell as gong.
units.literal: All use Yellow Bell as gong.

units.zh: 八曰舒和，以出入二舞，及皇太子、王公、羣后、國老若皇后之妾御、皇太子之宮臣，出入門則奏之。
units.en: VIII. Shuhe—for the two dances' entry and exit, and for the heir apparent, princes, consorts, state elders, the empress's attendants, and the heir apparent's palace officers as they pass through gates.
units.literal: Eighth Shuhe, for the two dances entering and leaving, and for the heir apparent, princes, consorts, state elders, the empress's attendants, and the heir apparent's palace officers when passing gates.

units.zh: 皆以太簇之商。
units.en: All use Taizu as shang.
units.literal: All use Taizu shang.

units.zh: 九曰昭和，皇帝、皇太子以舉酒。
units.en: IX. Zhaohe—emperor and heir raising the wine cup.
units.literal: Ninth Zhaohe, the emperor and heir apparent raising the cup.

units.zh: 十曰休和，皇帝以飯，以肅拜三老，皇太子亦以飯。
units.en: X. Xiuhe—imperial meal and bow to the Three Elders; heir's meal likewise.
units.literal: Tenth Xiuhe, the emperor at the meal, reverent bow to the Three Elders; the heir apparent also at the meal.

units.zh: 皆以其月之律均。
units.en: All follow the month's pitch jun.
units.literal: All use the month's pitch jun.

units.zh: 十一曰正和，皇后受冊以行。
units.en: XI. Zhenghe—empress receiving the seal in procession.
units.literal: Eleventh Zhenghe, the empress receiving the seal when proceeding.

units.zh: 十二曰承和，皇太子在其宮，有會以行。
units.en: XII. Chenghe—heir apparent's palace assemblies in procession.
units.literal: Twelfth Chenghe, the heir apparent in his palace when there is an assembly and he proceeds.

units.zh: 若駕出，則撞黃鍾，奏太和。
units.en: On imperial departure, Yellow Bell is struck and Taihe played.
units.literal: If the carriage goes out, Yellow Bell is struck and Taihe is played.

units.zh: 出太極門而奏采茨，至于嘉德門而止。
units.en: Leaving the Supreme Ultimate Gate, Caici plays until Jiade Gate, then ceases.
units.literal: Exiting the Supreme Ultimate Gate Caici is played until Jiade Gate, where it stops.

units.zh: 其還也亦然。
units.en: The return journey repeats the same.
units.literal: On return it is the same.

units.zh: 初，隋有文舞、武舞，至祖孝孫定樂，更文舞曰治康，武舞曰凱安，舞者各六十四人。
units.en: Sui had civil and martial dances; Zu Xiaosun renamed them Zhikang and Kai'an—sixty-four dancers each.
units.literal: At first Sui had civil and martial dances; when Zu Xiaosun fixed the music he changed civil dance to Zhikang and martial to Kai'an, sixty-four dancers each.

units.zh: 文舞：左籥右翟，與執纛而引者二人，皆委貌冠，黑素，絳領，廣袖，白絝，革帶，烏皮履。
units.en: Civil dance: yue left, di right; two banner bearers lead; weimao caps, black robes, crimson collars, broad sleeves, white trousers, leather belts, black shoes.
units.literal: Civil dance: left yue right di, with two bearing banners to lead, all wearing weimao caps, black plain cloth, crimson collars, broad sleeves, white ku, leather belts, black leather shoes.

units.zh: 武舞：左干右戚，執旌居前者二人，執鼗執鐸皆二人，金錞二，輿者四人，奏者二人，執鐃二人，執相在左，執雅在右，皆二人夾導，服平冕，餘同文舞。
units.en: Martial dance: shield left, axe right; flag, tao, duo, cymbal, and nao bearers; xiang left, ya right; pingmian caps; otherwise as civil dress.
units.literal: Martial dance: left shield right axe, two bearing flags before, two bearing tao and duo, two golden cymbals, four litter bearers, two performers, two naos, xiang left and ya right, two each flanking as guides, wearing pingmian caps, rest as civil dance.

units.zh: 朝會則武弁，平巾幘，廣袖，金甲，豹文絝，烏皮鞾。
units.en: Court audiences: martial caps, pingjin scarves, broad sleeves, golden armor, leopard-trimmed trousers, black boots.
units.literal: At court audiences martial caps, pingjin headcloth, broad sleeves, golden armor, leopard-pattern ku, black leather boots.

units.zh: 執干戚夾導，皆同郊廟。
units.en: Shield and axe guides as at suburban rites.
units.literal: Shield and axe bearers flanking as guides, all as at suburban altars.

units.zh: 凡初獻，作文舞之舞；
units.en: First offering: civil dance.
units.literal: For the first offering, perform the civil dance.

units.zh: 亞獻、終獻，作武舞之舞。
units.en: Second and final offerings: martial dance.
units.literal: Second and final offerings, perform the martial dance.

units.zh: 太廟降神以文舞，每室酌獻，各用其廟之舞。
units.en: Ancestral temple descent uses civil dance; each shrine's libation uses its own dance.
units.literal: Imperial temple spirit descent uses civil dance; each chamber's libation uses that temple's dance.

units.zh: 禘祫遷廟之主合食，則舞亦如之。
units.en: Combined di/xia feasts for relocated tablets follow the same rule.
units.literal: Di and xia when combined feasts for moved spirits, the dance is likewise.

units.zh: 儀鳳二年，太常卿韋萬石定凱安舞六變：一變象龍興參墟；
units.en: Yifeng year 2: Director Wei Wanshi set Kai'an in six variations—first, the dragon rising at Canxu.
units.literal: In the second year of Yifeng, Director Wei Wanshi fixed the Kai'an dance in six variations: first variation images the dragon rising at Canxu.

units.zh: 二變象克定關中；
units.en: Second: securing the Guanzhong passes.
units.literal: Second variation images securing the pass within.

units.zh: 三變象東夏賓服；
units.en: Third: eastern Xia's submission.
units.literal: Third variation images eastern Xia submitting.

units.zh: 四變象江淮平；
units.en: Fourth: pacifying the Jiang and Huai.
units.literal: Fourth variation images the Jiang-Huai pacified.

units.zh: 五變象獫狁伏從；
units.en: Fifth: the Xianyun subdued.
units.literal: Fifth variation images the Xianyun subdued.

units.zh: 六變復位以崇，象兵還振旅。
units.en: Sixth: returning to position, the army home and troops marshaled.
units.literal: Sixth returning to position to honor, images the army returning and marshaling troops.

units.zh: 初，太宗時，詔祕書監顏師古等撰定弘農府君至高祖太武皇帝六廟樂曲舞名，其後變更不一，而自獻祖而下廟舞，略可見也。
units.en: Taizong ordered Yan Shigu and others to name dances for six temples from the Lord of Hongnong through High Ancestor Emperor Taiwu; later names shifted, but from Offered Ancestor downward the temple dances can be traced.
units.literal: At first in Taizong's time an edict ordered Secretariat Director Yan Shigu and others to compile dance names for the six temples from the Lord of Hongnong through High Ancestor Emperor Taiwu; afterward changes were many, yet from Offered Ancestor down the temple dances can be seen in outline.

units.zh: 獻祖曰光大之舞，懿祖曰長發之舞，太祖曰大政之舞，世祖曰大成之舞，高祖曰大明之舞，太宗曰崇德之舞，高宗曰鈞天之舞，中宗曰太和之舞，睿宗曰景雲之舞，玄宗曰大運之舞，肅宗曰惟新之舞，代宗曰保大之舞，德宗曰文明之舞，順宗曰大順之舞，憲宗曰象德之舞，穆宗曰和寧之舞，敬宗曰大鈞之舞，文宗曰文成之舞，武宗曰大定之舞，昭宗曰咸寧之舞。
units.en: Offered Ancestor: Guangda; Respected Ancestor: Changfa; Great Ancestor: Dazheng; World Ancestor: Dacheng; High Ancestor: Daming; Taizong: Chongde; Gaozong: Juntian; Zhongzong: Taihe; Ruizong: Jingyun; Xuanzong: Dayun; Suzong: Weixin; Daizong: Baoda; Dezong: Wenming; Shunzong: Dashun; Xianzong: Xiangde; Muzong: Hening; Jingzong: Dajun; Wenzong: Wencheng; Wuzong: Dading; Zhaozong: Xianning.
units.literal: Offered Ancestor: Guangda; Respected Ancestor: Changfa; Great Ancestor: Dazheng; World Ancestor: Dacheng; High Ancestor: Daming; Taizong: Chongde; Gaozong: Juntian; Zhongzong: Taihe; Ruizong: Jingyun; Xuanzong: Dayun; Suzong: Weixin; Daizong: Baoda; Dezong: Wenming; Shunzong: Dashun; Xianzong: Xiangde; Muzong: Hening; Jingzong: Dajun; Wenzong: Wencheng; Wuzong: Dading; Zhaozong: Xianning.

units.zh: 其餘闕而不著。
units.en: Others are lost from the record.
units.literal: The rest are missing and not recorded.

units.zh: 唐之自製樂凡三：一曰七德舞，二曰九功舞，三日上元舞。
units.en: Tang composed three great dances: Seven Virtues, Nine Achievements, and Superior Prime.
units.literal: Tang's self-made music totals three: first the Seven Virtues dance, second the Nine Achievements dance, third the Superior Prime dance.

units.zh: 七德舞者，本名秦王破陣樂。
units.en: Seven Virtues was originally Prince of Qin Breaks the Array.
units.literal: The Seven Virtues dance was originally titled Prince of Qin Breaks the Array.

units.zh: 太宗為秦王，破劉武周，軍中相與作秦王破陣樂曲。
units.en: As Prince of Qin, Taizong defeated Liu Wuzhou; the army composed Prince of Qin Breaks the Array.
units.literal: When Taizong was Prince of Qin he defeated Liu Wuzhou; in the army they together made the Prince of Qin Breaks the Array tune.

units.zh: 及即位，宴會必奏之，謂侍臣曰：「雖發揚蹈厲，異乎文容，然功業由之，被於樂章，示不忘本也。」
units.en: On accession he played it at every feast, telling ministers: "Though fierce and stamping—not civil grace—merit born of war entered the repertoire; we must not forget our roots."
units.literal: When he took the throne, at every feast it was surely performed; he told his ministers: "Though it is vigorous and stamping, unlike civil bearing, yet merit arose from it and was spread in musical sections—showing not to forget the root."

units.zh: 右僕射封德彝曰：「陛下以聖武戡難，陳樂象德，文容豈足道也！」
units.en: Right Vice Director Feng Deyi said: "Your sagely martial prowess quelled chaos; music images virtue—civil grace alone cannot suffice!"
units.literal: Right Vice Director Feng Deyi said: "Your Majesty with sagely martial prowess quelled difficulty and set music imaging virtue—how can civil bearing suffice!"

units.zh: 帝矍然曰：「朕雖以武功興，終以文德綏海內，謂文容不如蹈厲，斯過矣。」
units.en: The emperor started: "I rose by arms yet ruled by wen; to call civil grace inferior to stamping—that goes too far."
units.literal: The emperor started and said: "I though I rose by martial prowess, in the end pacified the realm within by civil virtue; to say civil bearing is not as good as stamping—this is excessive."

units.zh: 乃製舞圖，左圓右方，先偏後伍，交錯屈伸，以象魚麗、鵝鸛。
units.en: He drafted a dance chart—round left, square right, echelons weaving like fish-scale and goose-wing formations.
units.literal: He then made a dance diagram—left round right square, first echelon then five, interlacing bending and stretching, to image fish-scale and goose formation.

units.zh: 命呂才以圖教樂工百二十八人，被銀甲執戟而舞，凡三變，每變為四陣，象擊刺往來，歌者和曰：「秦王破陣樂」。
units.en: Lü Cai taught 128 musicians in silver armor with halberds—three variations, four arrays each, miming battle; the chorus sang: "Prince of Qin Breaks the Array."
units.literal: He ordered Lü Cai to teach one hundred twenty-eight musicians by the diagram; clad in silver armor they grasped halberds and danced; three variations in all, each variation four arrays, imaging thrust and parry back and forth; singers harmonized: "Prince of Qin Breaks the Array."

units.zh: 後令魏徵與員外散騎常侍褚亮、員外散騎常侍虞世南、太子右庶子李百藥更製歌辭，名曰七德舞。
units.en: Later Wei Zheng, Chu Liang, Yu Shinan, and Li Baiyao rewrote the lyrics as Seven Virtues.
units.literal: Later he ordered Wei Zheng with Acting Palace Gentleman Chu Liang, Acting Palace Gentleman Yu Shinan, and Right Vice Director of the Heir Apparent Li Baiyao to remake the lyrics, titled Seven Virtues dance.

units.zh: 舞初成，觀者皆扼腕踊躍，諸將上壽，羣臣稱萬歲，蠻夷在庭者請相率以舞。
units.en: At the premiere viewers thumped their wrists and leaped; generals toasted; ministers cried "Ten thousand years!"; barbarian guests begged to join the dance.
units.literal: When the dance was first completed, viewers all clenched their wrists and leaped; generals offered longevity; ministers shouted ten thousand years; barbarians in the hall asked to dance together in succession.

units.zh: 太常卿蕭瑀曰：「樂所以美盛德形容，而有所未盡，陛下破劉武周、薛舉、竇建德、王世充，願圖其狀以識。」
units.en: Director Xiao Yu said: "Music should glorify virtue fully—yet victories over Liu Wuzhou, Xue Ju, Dou Jiande, and Wang Shichong remain undepicted; let us chart them."
units.literal: Director Xiao Yu said: "Music beautifies great virtue and appearance, yet something is not exhausted—Your Majesty defeated Liu Wuzhou, Xue Ju, Dou Jiande, and Wang Shichong; I wish to diagram their forms to remember."

units.zh: 帝曰：「方四海未定，攻伐以平禍亂，製樂陳其梗㮣而已。
units.en: The emperor said: "The four seas are not yet settled; attack and suppression to quell calamity and chaos—making music states the outline only.
units.literal: The emperor said: "The four seas are not yet settled; attack and suppression to quell calamity and chaos—making music states the hardship only.

units.zh: 若備寫禽獲，今將相有嘗為其臣者，觀之有所不忍，我不為也。」
units.en: To paint every captive would shame ministers who once served those foes—I will not."
units.literal: If I fully depicted those taken captive, now among generals and ministers some were once their subjects—viewing would be unbearable; I will not do it."

units.zh: 自是元日、冬至朝會慶賀，與九功舞同奏。
units.en: Thereafter New Year's and winter-solstice celebrations paired it with Nine Achievements.
units.literal: From then on at New Year's and winter solstice court congratulations and celebrations it was performed together with the Nine Achievements dance.

units.zh: 舞人更以進賢冠，虎文袴，螣蛇帶，烏皮鞾，二人執旌居前。
units.en: Dancers later wore jinxian caps, tiger-striped trousers, tengshe belts, black boots; two flag bearers led.
units.literal: Dancers later wore jinxian caps, tiger-pattern trousers, tengshe belts, black leather boots; two bore flags before.

units.zh: 其後更號神功破陣樂。
units.en: Later renamed Divine Merit Breaks the Array.
units.literal: Later it was renamed Divine Merit Breaks the Array.

units.zh: 九功舞者，本名功成慶善樂。
units.en: Nine Achievements was originally Merit Accomplished, Celebrating Goodness.
units.literal: The Nine Achievements dance was originally titled Merit Accomplished Celebrating Goodness.

units.zh: 太宗生於慶善宮，貞觀六年幸之，宴從臣，賞賜閭里，同漢沛、宛。
units.en: Taizong was born at Celebrating Goodness Palace; Zhenguan year 6 he visited, feasted followers, and rewarded the hamlet like Han at Pei and Wan.
units.literal: Taizong was born at Celebrating Goodness Palace; in the sixth year of Zhenguan he visited it, feasted his followers, rewarded the hamlet as Han did Pei and Wan.

units.zh: 帝歡甚，賦詩，起居郎呂才被之管絃，名曰功成慶善樂。
units.en: Delighted, he composed a poem; Lü Cai scored it as Merit Accomplished Celebrating Goodness Music.
units.literal: The emperor was very pleased and composed a poem; Attendant Gentleman Lü Cai set it to strings and pipes, titled Merit Accomplished Celebrating Goodness Music.

units.zh: 以童兒六十四人，冠進德冠，紫袴褶，長袖，漆髻，屣履而舞，號九功舞。
units.en: Sixty-four boys in jinde caps, purple jackets and trousers, long sleeves, lacquered topknots, slipper-shoes—the Nine Achievements dance.
units.literal: Sixty-four boys, jinde caps, purple trousers and jackets, long sleeves, lacquered topknots, slippers and shoes dancing, called Nine Achievements dance.

units.zh: 進蹈安徐，以象文德。
units.en: Their measured tread imaged civil virtue.
units.literal: Advancing with measured tread to image civil virtue.

units.zh: 麟德二年詔：「郊廟、享宴奏文舞，用功成慶善樂，曳履，執紼，服袴褶，童子冠如故。
units.en: Linde year 2 edict: "Suburban and feast civil dances use Merit Accomplished Celebrating Goodness—trailing shoes, cords, jackets, boys' caps unchanged.
units.literal: In the second year of Linde an edict: "Suburban altars and feasts perform civil dance with Merit Accomplished Celebrating Goodness Music, trailing shoes, holding cords, wearing trousers and jackets, boys' caps as before.

units.zh: 武舞用神功破陣樂，衣甲，持戟，執纛者被金甲，八佾，加簫、笛、歌鼓，列坐縣南，若舞即與宮縣合奏。
units.en: Martial dance uses Divine Merit Breaks the Array in armor with halberds; golden-armored banner bearers, eight rows, xiao, di, and song drums south of the stands—joining palace music when danced.
units.literal: Martial dance uses Divine Merit Breaks the Array, armored, holding halberds; banner bearers in golden armor, eight rows; adding xiao, di, and song drums, seated south of the stands; if dancing it joins the palace stands.

units.zh: 其宴樂二舞仍別設焉。」
units.en: Feast performances kept the two dances separate."
units.literal: The two feast dances were still set apart."

units.zh: 上元舞者，高宗所作也。
units.en: The Superior Prime dance was Gaozong's composition.
units.literal: The Superior Prime dance was made by Gaozong.

units.zh: 舞者百八十人，衣畫雲五色衣，以象元氣。
units.en: 180 dancers in painted five-colored cloud robes imaged primordial qi.
units.literal: One hundred eighty dancers wore painted cloud five-colored robes to image primordial qi.

units.zh: 其樂有上元、二儀、三才、四時、五行、六律、七政、八風、九宮、十洲、得一、慶雲之曲，大祠享皆用之。
units.en: Its repertoire included Superior Prime, Two Principles, Three Powers, Four Seasons, Five Phases, Six Pipes, Seven Regulators, Eight Winds, Nine Palaces, Ten Isles, Obtaining the One, and Celebrating Cloud—used at major sacrifices.
units.literal: Its music had Superior Prime, Two Principles, Three Powers, Four Seasons, Five Phases, Six Pitch Pipes, Seven Regulators, Eight Winds, Nine Palaces, Ten Isles, Obtaining the One, and Celebrating Cloud pieces—great sacrifices all used them.

units.zh: 至上元三年，詔：「惟圓丘、方澤、太廟乃用，餘皆罷。」
units.en: Shangyuan year 3 edict: "Only Round Mound, Square Mound, and Ancestral Temple retain them; all else abolished."
units.literal: By the third year of Shangyuan an edict: "Only the Round Mound, Square Mound, and Imperial Ancestral Temple use them; the rest are all stopped."

units.zh: 又曰：「神功破陣樂不入雅樂，功成慶善樂不可降神，亦皆罷。」
units.en: It also said: "Divine Merit Breaks the Array was barred from elegant music; Merit Accomplished Celebrating Goodness could not bring spirits down—both abolished."
units.literal: It also said: "Divine Merit Breaks the Array does not enter elegant music; Merit Accomplished Celebrating Goodness cannot bring down spirits—both are also stopped."

units.zh: 而郊廟用治康、凱安如故。
units.en: Suburban rites still used Zhikang and Kai'an.
units.literal: Yet suburban altars used Zhikang and Kai'an as before.

units.zh: 儀鳳二年，太常卿韋萬石奏：「請作上元舞，兼奏破陣、慶善二舞。
units.en: Yifeng year 2: Director Wei Wanshi memorialized: "I ask to perform Superior Prime alongside Breaks the Array and Celebrating Goodness.
units.literal: In the second year of Yifeng, Director Wei Wanshi memorialized: "I request making the Superior Prime dance while also performing Breaks the Array and Celebrating Goodness.

units.zh: 而破陣樂五十二徧，著于雅樂者二徧；
units.en: Breaks the Array ran fifty-two repetitions, two in elegant music.
units.literal: Breaks the Array music fifty-two repetitions, two recorded in elegant music.

units.zh: 慶善樂五十徧，著于雅樂者一徧；
units.en: Celebrating Goodness fifty, one in elegant music.
units.literal: Celebrating Goodness music fifty repetitions, one in elegant music.

units.zh: 上元舞二十九徧，皆著于雅樂。」
units.en: Superior Prime twenty-nine, all in elegant music."
units.literal: Superior Prime dance twenty-nine repetitions, all in elegant music."

units.zh: 又曰：「雲門、大咸、大㲈、大夏，古文舞也。
units.en: He also said: "Cloud Gate, Great Xian, Great Zhi, and Great Xia were ancient civil dances.
units.literal: He also said: "Cloud Gate, Great Xian, Great Zhi, and Great Xia are ancient civil dances.

units.zh: 大濩、大武，古武舞也。
units.en: Great Huo and Great Martial were ancient martial dances.
units.literal: Great Huo and Great Martial are ancient martial dances.

units.zh: 為國家者，揖讓得天下，則先奏文舞；
units.en: States born of yielding play civil dance first.
units.literal: For a state, if yielding and declining obtain the realm, civil dance is performed first.

units.zh: 征伐得天下，則先奏武舞。
units.en: States born of conquest play martial dance first.
units.literal: If campaign and conquest obtain the realm, martial dance is performed first.

units.zh: 神功破陣樂有武事之象，功成慶善樂有文事之象，用二舞，請先奏神功破陣樂。」
units.en: Breaks the Array images war; Celebrating Goodness images wen—please play Breaks the Array first."
units.literal: Divine Merit Breaks the Array has the image of martial affairs; Merit Accomplished Celebrating Goodness has the image of civil affairs—using the two dances, I request performing Divine Merit Breaks the Array first.

units.zh: 初，朝會常奏破陣舞，高宗即位，不忍觀之，乃不設。
units.en: Early audiences always played Breaks the Array; Gaozong, unable to watch, discontinued it.
units.literal: At first court audiences always performed Breaks the Array; when Gaozong took the throne he could not bear to watch and it was not set up.

units.zh: 後幸九成宮，置酒，韋萬石曰：「破陣樂舞，所以宣揚祖宗盛烈，以示後世，自陛下即位，寢而不作者久矣。
units.en: At Jiucheng Palace, Wei Wanshi urged: "Breaks the Array proclaims ancestral glory—unused since Your Majesty's accession.
units.literal: Later the emperor visited Jiucheng Palace and set out wine; Wei Wanshi said: "Breaks the Array dance propagates the ancestors' great splendor to show posterity; since Your Majesty's accession it has long lain unused.

units.zh: 禮，天子親總干戚，以舞先祖之樂。
units.en: Rites require the Son of Heaven himself to dance ancestral music with shield and axe.
units.literal: Rites say the Son of Heaven personally wields shield and axe to dance the ancestors' music.

units.zh: 今破陣樂久廢，羣下無所稱述，非所以發孝思也。」
units.en: Its long silence leaves the court mute—hardly filial remembrance."
units.literal: Now Breaks the Array music has long been abandoned; below there is nothing to proclaim—this is not how to express filial thought."

units.zh: 帝復令奏之，舞畢，歎曰：「不見此樂垂三十年，追思王業勤勞若此，朕安可忘武功邪！」
units.en: The emperor restored it; when it ended he sighed: "Thirty years without this dance—such toil! How could I forget martial merit?"
units.literal: The emperor again ordered it performed; when the dance ended he sighed: "Not to see this music for thirty years—recalling the royal enterprise's toil thus, how can I forget martial achievement!"

units.zh: 羣臣皆稱萬歲。
units.en: Ministers cried ten thousand years.
units.literal: The ministers all shouted ten thousand years.

units.zh: 然遇饗燕奏二樂，天子必避位，坐者皆興。
units.en: At feasts playing both dances the emperor left his seat and all stood.
units.literal: Yet when feasts played the two dances the Son of Heaven always left his seat and those seated all rose.

units.zh: 太常博士裴守真以謂「奏二舞時，天子不宜起立」。
units.en: Doctor Pei Shouzhen held that "when the two dances are played, the emperor should not rise."
units.literal: Court of Imperial Sacrifices Doctor Pei Shouzhen held that when the two dances play the Son of Heaven should not rise.

units.zh: 詔從之。
units.en: An edict agreed.
units.literal: An edict followed this.

units.zh: 及高宗崩，改治康舞曰化康以避諱。
units.en: After Gaozong's death Zhikang became Huakang to avoid his name.
units.literal: When Gaozong died Zhikang dance was changed to Huakang to avoid the taboo.

units.zh: 武后毀唐太廟，七德、九功之舞皆亡，唯其名存。
units.en: Empress Wu wrecked the Tang ancestral temple; Seven Virtues and Nine Achievements vanished—names alone survived.
units.literal: Empress Wu destroyed Tang's Imperial Ancestral Temple; the Seven Virtues and Nine Achievements dances were all lost—only their names remain.

units.zh: 自後復用隋文舞、武舞而已。
units.en: Thereafter only Sui's civil and martial dances returned.
units.literal: Afterward Sui civil and martial dances alone were used again.

units.zh: 燕樂。
units.en: Banquet music (yan yue).
units.literal: Banquet music.

units.zh: 高祖即位，仍隋制設九部樂：燕樂伎，樂工舞人無變者。
units.en: Gaozu kept Sui's Nine Department Music; Yan Music performers unchanged.
units.literal: When Gaozu took the throne he still followed Sui in establishing the Nine Department Music: Yan Music performers, musicians and dancers unchanged.

units.zh: 清商伎者，隋清樂也。
units.en: Pure Shang was Sui court music.
units.literal: Pure Shang performers were Sui's pure music.

units.zh: 有編鍾、編磬、獨絃琴、擊琴、瑟、秦琵琶、臥箜篌、筑、箏、節鼓，皆一；
units.en: One each: serial bells and chimes, solo-string qin, struck qin, se, Qin pipa, horizontal konghou, zhu, zheng, marking drum.
units.literal: Serial bells, serial chimes, solo-string qin, struck qin, se, Qin pipa, horizontal konghou, zhu, zheng, marking drum—each one.

units.zh: 笙、笛、簫、篪、方響、跋膝，皆二。
units.en: Two each: sheng, di, xiao, chi, fangxiang, baxi.
units.literal: Sheng, di, xiao, chi, fangxiang, baxi—each two.

units.zh: 歌二人，吹葉一人，舞者四人，幷習巴渝舞。
units.en: Two singers, one leaf-blower, four dancers—all trained in Ba-Yu dance.
units.literal: Two singers, one leaf-blower, four dancers, all practicing Ba-Yu dance.

units.zh: 西涼伎，有編鍾、編磬，皆一；
units.en: Western Liang: one each serial bells and chimes.
units.literal: Western Liang performers: serial bells and chimes each one.

units.zh: 彈箏、搊箏、臥箜篌、豎箜篌、琵琶、五絃、笙、簫、觱篥、小觱篥、笛、橫笛、腰鼓、齊鼓、檐鼓，皆一；
units.en: One each: plucked and strummed zheng, konghou, pipa, five-string, sheng, xiao, bili large and small, di, transverse di, waist, Qi, and eaves drums.
units.literal: Plucked zheng, strummed zheng, horizontal and vertical konghou, pipa, five-string, sheng, xiao, bili, small bili, di, transverse di, waist drum, Qi drum, eaves drum—each one.

units.zh: 銅鈸二，貝一。
units.en: Two bronze cymbals, one shell horn.
units.literal: Two bronze cymbals, one shell.

units.zh: 白舞一人，方舞四人。
units.en: One white dance, four square dance.
units.literal: One white dance, four square dance.

units.zh: 天竺伎，有銅鼓、羯鼓、都曇鼓、毛員鼓、觱篥、橫笛、鳳首箜篌、琵琶、五絃、貝，皆一；
units.en: Indic: one each bronze, jie, Dutun, Maoyuan drums, bili, transverse di, phoenix konghou, pipa, five-string, shell.
units.literal: Indic performers: bronze drum, jie drum, Dutun drum, Maoyuan drum, bili, transverse di, phoenix-head konghou, pipa, five-string, shell—each one.

units.zh: 銅鈸二，舞者二人。
units.en: Two cymbals, two dancers.
units.literal: Two bronze cymbals, two dancers.

units.zh: 高麗伎，有彈箏、搊箏、鳳首箜篌、臥箜篌、豎箜篌、琵琶，以蛇皮為槽，厚寸餘，有鱗甲，楸木為面，象牙為捍撥，畫國王形。
units.en: Koryo: plucked and strummed zheng, phoenix and horizontal konghou, pipa with snake-skin box an inch thick scaled, catalpa face, ivory guard painted with the king.
units.literal: Koryo performers: plucked zheng, strummed zheng, phoenix konghou, horizontal and vertical konghou, pipa with snake-skin soundbox an inch thick with scale pattern, catalpa face, ivory plectrum guard painted with the king's image.

units.zh: 又有五絃、義觜笛、笙、葫蘆笙、簫、小觱篥、桃皮觱篥、腰鼓、齊鼓、檐鼓、龜頭鼓、鐵版、貝、大觱篥。
units.en: Also five-string, yizui di, sheng, gourd sheng, xiao, bili large and small, many drums, iron clapper, shell, great bili.
units.literal: Also five-string, yizui di, sheng, gourd sheng, xiao, small bili, peach-skin bili, waist, Qi, eaves, turtle-head, and great drums, iron clapper, shell, great bili.

units.zh: 胡旋舞，舞者立毬上，旋轉如風。
units.en: Hu Xuan dance: dancers spin atop a ball like wind.
units.literal: Hu Xuan dance: dancers stand on a ball and spin like wind.

units.zh: 龜茲伎，有彈箏、豎箜篌、琵琶、五絃、橫笛、笙、簫、觱篥、答臘鼓、毛員鼓、都曇鼓、侯提鼓、雞婁鼓、腰鼓、齊鼓、檐鼓、貝，皆一；
units.en: Kucha: one each plucked zheng, vertical konghou, pipa, five-string, transverse di, sheng, xiao, bili, dalagu, Maoyuan, Dutun, houti, jilou, waist, Qi, eaves drums, shell.
units.literal: Kucha performers: plucked zheng, vertical konghou, pipa, five-string, transverse di, sheng, xiao, bili, dalagu, Maoyuan, Dutun, houti, jilou, waist, Qi, eaves drums, shell—each one.

units.zh: 銅鈸二。
units.en: Two bronze cymbals.
units.literal: Two bronze cymbals.

units.zh: 舞者四人。
units.en: Four dancers.
units.literal: Four dancers.

units.zh: 設五方師子，高丈餘，飾以方色。
units.en: Five directional lions over a zhang tall, colored by direction.
units.literal: Five direction lions over a zhang high, decorated in directional colors.

units.zh: 每師子有十二人，畫衣，執紅拂，首加紅袜，謂之師子郎。
units.en: Twelve painted robe bearers with red whisks and red socks per lion—"lion lads."
units.literal: Each lion had twelve men in painted robes holding red whisks, red socks on the head, called lion lads.

units.zh: 安國伎，有豎箜篌、琵琶、五絃、橫笛、簫、觱篥、正鼓、和鼓、銅鈸，皆一；
units.en: Anguo: one each vertical konghou, pipa, five-string, transverse di, xiao, bili, zheng and he drums, cymbal.
units.literal: Anguo performers: vertical konghou, pipa, five-string, transverse di, xiao, bili, zheng drum, he drum, bronze cymbal—each one.

units.zh: 舞者二人。
units.en: Two dancers.
units.literal: Two dancers.

units.zh: 疏勒伎，有豎箜篌、琵琶、五絃、簫、橫笛、觱篥、答臘鼓、羯鼓、侯提鼓、腰鼓、雞婁鼓，皆一；
units.en: Shule: one each vertical konghou, pipa, five-string, xiao, transverse di, bili, dalagu, jie, houti, waist, jilou drums.
units.literal: Shule performers: vertical konghou, pipa, five-string, xiao, transverse di, bili, dalagu, jie, houti, waist, jilou drums—each one.

units.zh: 舞者二人。
units.en: Two dancers.
units.literal: Two dancers.

units.zh: 康國伎，有正鼓、和鼓，皆一；
units.en: Kangju: one each zheng and he drums.
units.literal: Kangju performers: zheng and he drums each one.

units.zh: 笛、銅鈸，皆二。
units.en: Two each di and cymbals.
units.literal: Di and bronze cymbals each two.

units.zh: 舞者二人。
units.en: Two dancers.
units.literal: Two dancers.

units.zh: 工人之服皆從其國。
units.en: Musicians dressed in their native styles.
units.literal: Workers' dress followed their countries.

units.zh: 隋樂每奏九部樂終，輒奏文康樂，一曰禮畢。
units.en: After each Nine Department set Sui played Wenkang—"Rite Complete."
units.literal: Sui music after each Nine Department performance always played Wenkang music, also called Rite Complete.

units.zh: 太宗時，命削去之，其後遂亡。
units.en: Taizong abolished it; the piece then vanished.
units.literal: In Taizong's time an order cut it out; afterward it perished.

units.zh: 及平高昌，收其樂。
units.en: Pacifying Gaochang brought its music into court.
units.literal: When Gaochang was pacified its music was received.

units.zh: 有豎箜篌、銅角，一；
units.en: One each vertical konghou and bronze horn.
units.literal: Vertical konghou and bronze horn, one each.

units.zh: 琵琶、五絃、橫笛、簫、觱篥、答臘鼓、腰鼓、雞婁鼓、羯鼓，皆二人。
units.en: Two each pipa, five-string, transverse di, xiao, bili, dalagu, waist, jilou, jie drums.
units.literal: Pipa, five-string, transverse di, xiao, bili, dalagu, waist, jilou, jie drums—each two.

units.zh: 工人布巾，袷袍，錦襟，金銅帶，畫絝。
units.en: Musicians: cloth headwrap, lined robe, brocade collar, gilt belt, painted trousers.
units.literal: Workers: cloth headcloth, lined robe, brocade collar, bronze-gold belt, painted ku.

units.zh: 舞者二人，黃袍袖，練襦，五色絛帶，金銅耳璫，赤鞾。
units.en: Two dancers in yellow sleeves, white jacket, five-color sash, gilt earrings, red boots.
units.literal: Two dancers: yellow sleeves, white jacket, five-colored sash, gilt ear pendants, red boots.

units.zh: 自是初有十部樂。
units.en: Thus Ten Department Music began.
units.literal: From this the Ten Department Music first appeared.

units.zh: 其後因內宴，詔長孫无忌製傾盃曲，魏徵製樂社樂曲，虞世南製英雄樂曲。
units.en: Later at a palace feast an edict ordered Zhangsun Wuji to compose Tilting Cup, Wei Zheng to compose Music Society, and Yu Shinan to compose Hero.
units.literal: Later at an inner feast an edict ordered Zhangsun Wuji to compose Tilting Cup, Wei Zheng to compose Music Society, Yu Shinan to compose Hero.

units.zh: 帝之破竇建德也，乘馬名黃驄驃，及征高麗，死於道，頗哀惜之，命樂工製黃驄疊曲。
units.en: When the emperor defeated Dou Jiande, his mount was Yellow Cong Biao; it later died on the Goryeo campaign, and he grieved enough to have musicians compose Yellow Cong Layered Tune.
units.literal: When the emperor defeated Dou Jiande he rode a horse named Yellow Cong Biao; on the Liaodong campaign it died on the road; deeply mourned, he ordered musicians to compose Yellow Cong Layered tune.

units.zh: 四曲，皆宮調也。
units.en: Four pieces, all gong mode.
units.literal: Four pieces, all in gong mode.

units.zh: 五絃，如琵琶而小，北國所出，舊以木撥彈，樂工裴神符初以手彈，太宗悅甚，後人習為搊琵琶。
units.en: Five-string—a small northern pipa once wood-plucked until Pei Shenfu played with fingers; Taizong delighted; later called strummed pipa.
units.literal: Five-string: like pipa but smaller, from the northern states; formerly plucked with wood; musician Pei Shenfu first plucked by hand; Taizong was very pleased; later men practiced it as strummed pipa.

units.zh: 高宗即位，景雲見，河水清，張文收采古誼為景雲河清歌，亦名燕樂。
units.en: Gaozong's accession brought auspicious clouds and a clear Yellow River; Zhang Wenshou composed Jingyun River Clear song—also Yan Music.
units.literal: When Gaozong took the throne auspicious clouds appeared and the Yellow River cleared; Zhang Wenshou gathered ancient meaning for Jingyun River Clear song, also called Yan Music.

units.zh: 有玉磬、方響、搊箏、筑、臥箜篌、大小箜篌、大小琵琶、大小五絃、吹葉、大小笙、大小觱篥、簫、銅鈸、長笛、尺八、短笛，皆一；
units.en: One each: jade qing, fangxiang, strummed zheng, zhu, konghou, pipa, five-string, leaf-blowing, sheng, bili, xiao, cymbals, long di, shakuhachi, short di.
units.literal: Jade qing, fangxiang, strummed zheng, zhu, horizontal konghou large and small, pipa large and small, five-string large and small, leaf-blowing, sheng large and small, bili large and small, xiao, bronze cymbals, long di, shakuhachi, short di—each one.

units.zh: 毛員鼓、連鞉鼓、桴鼓、貝，皆二。
units.en: Two each Maoyuan drum, linked tambourine, mallet drum, shell.
units.literal: Maoyuan drum, linked tambourine, mallet drum, shell—each two.

units.zh: 每器工一人，歌二人。
units.en: One musician per instrument, two singers.
units.literal: One musician per instrument, two singers.

units.zh: 工人絳袍，金帶，烏鞾。
units.en: Musicians in crimson robes, gold belts, black boots.
units.literal: Workers: crimson robe, gold belt, black boots.

units.zh: 舞者二十人。
units.en: Twenty dancers.
units.literal: Twenty dancers.

units.zh: 分四部：一景雲舞，二慶善舞，三破陣舞，四承天舞。
units.en: Four sections: Jingyun, Celebrating Goodness, Breaks the Array, Receiving Heaven dances.
units.literal: Divided in four sections: first Jingyun dance, second Celebrating Goodness, third Breaks the Array, fourth Receiving Heaven.

units.zh: 景雲樂，舞八人，五色雲冠，錦袍，五色袴，金銅帶。
units.en: Jingyun: eight dancers in five-color cloud caps, brocade robes and trousers, gilt belts.
units.literal: Jingyun music: eight dancers, five-colored cloud caps, brocade robes, five-colored trousers, bronze-gold belts.

units.zh: 慶善樂，舞四人，紫袍，白袴。
units.en: Celebrating Goodness: four in purple robes, white trousers.
units.literal: Celebrating Goodness: four dancers, purple robes, white trousers.

units.zh: 破陣樂，舞四人，綾袍，絳袴。
units.en: Breaks the Array: four in damask robes, crimson trousers.
units.literal: Breaks the Array: four dancers, damask robes, crimson trousers.

units.zh: 承天樂，舞四人，進德冠，紫袍，白袴。
units.en: Receiving Heaven: four in jinde caps, purple robes, white trousers.
units.literal: Receiving Heaven: four dancers, jinde caps, purple robes, white trousers.

units.zh: 景雲舞，元會第一奏之。
units.en: Jingyun dance opened the New Year assembly.
units.literal: Jingyun dance was performed first at the New Year assembly.

units.zh: 高宗以琴曲寖絕，雖有傳者，復失宮商，令有司脩習。
units.en: Gaozong found qin repertoire fading; surviving pieces had lost proper modes—he ordered restoration.
units.literal: Gaozong held qin pieces were gradually lost; though some were transmitted they again lost gong and shang; he ordered the authorities to repair and practice.

units.zh: 太常丞呂才上言：「舜彈五絃之琴，歌南風之詩，是知琴操曲弄皆合於歌。
units.en: Assistant Director Lü Cai argued: "Shun's five-string qin and Southern Winds show melodies must match lyrics.
units.literal: Court of Imperial Sacrifices Assistant Director Lü Cai memorialized: "Shun played the five-string qin and sang the Southern Winds poem—thus qin melodies and pieces all accord with song.

units.zh: 今以御雪詩為白雪歌。
units.en: He set the Imperial Snow poem as White Snow song.
units.literal: Now take the Imperial Snow poem as White Snow song.

units.zh: 古今奏正曲復有送聲，君唱臣和之義，以羣臣所和詩十六韻為送聲十六節。」
units.en: Proper pieces include 'sending voice'—lord sings, ministers answer; sixteen rhymes of minister poetry became sixteen sending sections."
units.literal: Ancient and modern in performing proper pieces there is also sending voice—the lord sings and ministers harmonize; take the ministers' harmonizing poem of sixteen rhymes as sending voice in sixteen sections."

units.zh: 帝善之，乃命太常著于樂府。
units.en: The emperor approved; the Court entered it in the Music Bureau.
units.literal: The emperor approved and ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to record it in the Music Bureau.

units.zh: 才復撰琴歌、白雪等曲，帝亦製歌詞十六，皆著樂府。
units.en: Cai composed qin songs including White Snow; the emperor added sixteen lyrics—all filed in the Music Bureau.
units.literal: Cai further composed qin songs White Snow and the like; the emperor also composed sixteen lyrics, all recorded in the Music Bureau.

units.zh: 帝將伐高麗，燕洛陽城門，觀屯營教舞，按新征用武之勢，名曰一戎大定樂，舞者百四十人，被五采甲，持槊而舞，歌者和之曰：「八紘同軌樂。」
units.en: Before the Goryeo campaign he feasted at Luoyang's gate, watching drill dances; he named One Military Great Settlement Music—140 armored dancers with spears; the chorus sang: "Eight Directions Same Track Music."
units.literal: The emperor was about to campaign Goryeo and feasted at Luoyang city gate, viewing encampment drill dance; following the new expedition's martial bearing he titled it One Military Great Settlement Music—140 dancers in five-colored armor dancing with spears; singers harmonized: "Eight Directions Same Track Music."

units.zh: 象高麗平而天下大定也。
units.en: It imaged Goryeo subdued and the realm settled.
units.literal: Imaging Goryeo pacified and the realm greatly settled.

units.zh: 及遼東平，行軍大總管李勣作夷美賓之曲以獻。
units.en: After Liaodong fell, Li Ji presented the Yimei Guest piece.
units.literal: When Liaodong was pacified Campaign Commander Li Ji composed the Yimei Guest piece and presented it.

units.zh: 調露二年，幸洛陽城南樓，宴羣臣，太常奏六合還淳之舞，其容制不傳。
units.en: Tiaolu year 2, at Luoyang's south tower feast, the Court played Six Harmonies Return to Purity—its choreography unrecorded.
units.literal: In the second year of Tiaolu, visiting the south tower of Luoyang, feasting ministers, the Court performed the Six Harmonies Return to Purity dance; its form is not transmitted.

units.zh: 高宗自以李氏老子之後也，於是命樂工製道調。
units.en: Gaozong, claiming descent from Laozi, ordered musicians to compose Dao mode.
units.literal: Gaozong held himself descendant of the Li clan and Laozi and therefore ordered musicians to compose Dao mode.
